published_statement: CODATA 2022 Table (2409.03787, READ): 'speed of light in vacuum c 299 792 458 m s^-1 exact'; 'Newtonian constant of gravitation G 6.674 30(15) x 10^-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2, 2.2 x 10^-5'; 'Planck constant h 6.626 070 15 x 10^-34 J Hz^-1 exact; hbar 1.054 571 817 ... x 10^-34 J s exact'; Planck length (hbar G/c^3)^(1/2) = 1.616 255(18) x 10^-35 m (NIST 2022 table; identical in 2018); Sec. I.B.11: 'Since there is no new value, the same 3.9 expansion factor applied to their uncertainties in 2018 ... is also used in 2022; the 2022 and 2018 recommended values of G are therefore identical.' Reyle+2021 Table 1 (READ): Proxima Cen 'EPOCH 2016.0', 'PARALLAX 768.066539187357' mas, 'PARALLAX_ERROR 0.049872905', bibcode 2020yCat.1350 (Gaia EDR3). IAU 2015 B3 (READ): '1 R^N_sun = 6.957 x 10^8 m'. No source states 4.2465 ly: that is the tree's 1/parallax, which re-derives to 4.2464599 ly at J2016.0.
published_hypotheses: c and h are exact by definition (SI 2019); hbar = h/(2 pi) is exact but irrational, so any decimal literal truncates it.
G is a measured value from 16 mutually inconsistent inputs; its u_r 2.2e-5 already carries a 3.9 expansion factor (CODATA 2022 Sec. I.B.11, READ).
l_P is derived, (hbar G/c^3)^(1/2), so its uncertainty (1.1e-5) is half of G's.

The Gaia parallax is barycentric, at epoch J2016.0, with formal uncertainty 0.0499 mas (6.5e-5 relative); it is not zero-point corrected in the catalogue, and Proxima's colour lies outside the Lindegren+2021 correction's validity (READ in the sibling audit gaia-dr3-proxima-distance).
Distance = 1/parallax, a light year = c x Julian year, so 'light time in years' equals 'distance in ly' only in Julian years and only at the stated epoch.
R^N_sun is a nominal conversion constant ('not ... the true solar properties'); the solar mass in kg is not nominal but GM^N/G, carrying G's uncertainty (IAU 2015 B3 Recommends 5).

NONE for the D7 figure's constants (specthm.py:461-467 S_closed): c, G, hbar, FEWSTER_C are used in the sense the sources define; FEWSTER_C = mu_1^4/(16 pi^2) recomputes to 3.169857938310468 (rel 3.6e-16). The physical hypotheses of the QEI (massless minimally coupled scalar, Hadamard, flat) belong to the 1208.5399 entry, not to this one.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested here: evidence both ways, and the answer for this entry is that later data move printed digits, never a conclusion. FOR: two of these data have moved since first measured and one is still internally contested. The Proxima parallax moved from Gaia DR2 768.529 to DR3 768.066 mas (-0.46 mas, 2.05 combined sigma; the distance by +6e-4), and the tree's own printed '4.247 years' is not fixed by the current datum (4.246 on the unrounded value, on today's epoch and at the low 1-sigma end); Gaia DR4 (expected ca. Dec 2026, READ in 2512.08533) may move it again. G's recommended value changed 2006->2010->2014->2018 by up to 7e-5 and its 16 inputs disagree enough to need a 3.9 expansion factor -- the physicists did lack consistent data, and CODATA says so. AGAINST: none of it reaches a conclusion the tree draws from these numbers. The D7 figure S1 = 1.8e71 moves 3e-5 orders across every G since 2006; c and h are exact by definition since 2019, so no future datum can move them; l_P inherits only G's half-uncertainty; the Rec setup time moves by <= 6.1e-4 relative across every datum read; the S-1 focal length is ~550 AU under every input. The only things new data change are the 4th printed figure of the Proxima light time and the 6th printed figure of the exchange rate.
grade_evidence: The constants STAND: c, G, hbar (truncated at -6.1e-10), l_P equal CODATA 2018 = CODATA 2022 exactly (READ in the 2022 paper text and the NIST tables), FEWSTER_C recomputes to 3.6e-16, and the D7 figure log10 S1 = 71.2557 moves <= 3.8e-5 orders under any G ever recommended or +-3.9 sigma (script RC 0). NARROWED, not STANDS, because the tree drops hypotheses the Proxima datum and G carry, each measured here: (i) epoch -- the 4.2465 ly is the J2016.0 barycentric distance; at 2026-09-26 it is 4.24566 ly; (ii) precision -- specthm.py:753 prints '4.247 years' by re-rounding the 5-s.f. 4.2465, while the datum 4.24646 prints 4.246 and the formal 1-sigma interval spans both, so the printed 4th figure is not a measured figure; (iii) specthm.py:1243 prints the exchange rate to 6 figures, the 6th not fixed by G at 1 sigma. Recorded discrepancies, none a refutation and none repaired: spec.py's Sun mass 1.989e30 is +2.97e-4 from GM^N/G (outside u(G); a rounding) giving f_sun 547.595 vs 547.758 AU, both '~550'; spec.LIGHT_YEAR and spec.AU are roundings (-3.2e-6, +2.0e-7). No moved or contested datum moves any verdict, refusal or witness: the narrowing is of the class of statements the numbers support (~4 s.f. at a stated epoch; 5 s.f. for G-dependent magnitudes), not of the tree's conclusions. Limitation named: the later-literature search could not run (alphaXiv quota), so 'no newer datum' is established only through CODATA 2022 and the 2025 HST parallax.
what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS if the owners carried the epoch (J2016.0) and printed the Proxima light time at the precision the datum fixes (4.246 +- 0.0003, or 3 s.f. 4.25) and the exchange rate at <= 5 figures -- i.e. the narrowing is about what the printed figures claim, and would vanish with them. DATA-DEPENDENT only if a verdict came to hinge on the 4th figure of the Proxima distance or on G below 1e-4 -- none does (S1 has 71 orders of margin). WRONG only if a literal were shown to differ from its source beyond rounding (none does: 6/6 constants and the parallax reproduce). Gaia DR4 (ca. Dec 2026) moving the parallax by more than ~0.2 mas would change the printed figure again, not the conclusion.
